title: Losing track of time, happily
text: Most of us know the feeling {{1}} hours vanish: the climb, the code, the chapter that swallowed an evening. Psychologists call {{2}} 'flow', and it occurs when a task sits in the narrow band where difficulty matches skill — neither {{3}} easy nor too hard. {{4}} is the absorption that makes flow so valuable: self-consciousness fades, feedback is instant, {{5}} the activity becomes its own reward. Such is the pull {{6}} people report losing track of hunger, weather and, famously, of time itself. Flow cannot be bought or scheduled directly, {{7}} conditions can be arranged: clear goals, uninterrupted stretches and challenges at the edge of ability. What employers are slowly learning is that the deepest satisfaction at work comes not from ease {{8}} from absorption.
